title: Status endpoints and public status feed
goal: Serve the health and status endpoints of the API app: `/healthz`, `/readyz` and the cached public `/v1/status` feed with components, incidents, minimum client version, contract version and deprecations.
scope_in: `GET /healthz` (always `200 {"status":"ok"}`, touches no dependency) and `GET /readyz` (DB, Redis and migration-version checks, `503 {"status":"degraded","checks":{...}}` on failure).
Component registry from config `STATUS_COMPONENTS` (id, name, probe URL or Redis heartbeat key) and a prober with 2 s timeout, results memoised 15 s in Redis so all instances agree.
Tables `status_incidents` and `status_incident_updates` plus a service API for B087 to create/update incidents; table `status_deprecations`.

`min_client_version` read from Redis key `status:min_client_version` (written by the release service) with fallback to config `MIN_CLIENT_VERSION`; `contract_version` read from the bundled `contracts/index.json` at build time.
scope_out: Relay process health and graceful shutdown (B037).
Admin endpoints and UI to manage incidents (B087, B088).
build_against: Postgres/Redis containers from B010; component probes are pointed at a scripted local HTTP server (up/slow/down); contract version is read from the repo's `contracts/index.json`.
interfaces: `statusService.createIncident({title, component_ids, status}): Promise<Incident>`, `addIncidentUpdate(id, text, status?)`, `resolveIncident(id)`, `setDeprecation({what, sunset})`.
Redis key `status:min_client_version`; cache keys `status:probe:{component}` TTL 15 s.
acceptance: `/healthz` returns 200 `{"status":"ok"}` in < 5 ms p99 and still returns 200 when Postgres and Redis are stopped.

`/readyz` returns 200 only if a `SELECT 1` (<= 1 s), a Redis `PING` (<= 1 s) and the migration table version equals the expected version all succeed; otherwise 503 with `checks` naming each failed check as `{ok:false}` and no error strings, hostnames or stack traces.

`/v1/status` validates against the CT-STATUS shape; with one component `major_outage` the overall status is `major_outage`; with one `degraded` and the rest `operational` it is `degraded`; a component probe failing 3 consecutive times becomes `major_outage`, one failure `degraded`.
Repeated calls within 15 s trigger at most one probe round per component cluster-wide (verified with two app instances and a probe counter).
`Cache-Control: public, max-age=15` and `ETag` are present; `If-None-Match` yields 304; response size <= 32 KiB with 50 components and 20 incidents.
An open incident appears in `incidents[]` with its ordered `updates[]`; a resolved incident older than 7 days is omitted.
`min_client_version` reflects the Redis key within 15 s; if absent the config value is used; `contract_version` equals `contract_version` in `contracts/index.json`.
`/v1/status` is available without authentication and, under a DB outage, still responds 200 from the last cached snapshot (up to 5 min) flagged by `updated_at`.
tests: unit: worst-of aggregation; probe failure counting; incident ordering and expiry filter.
integration: readiness with each dependency down, and with a pending migration.
contract: `/v1/status` body vs CT-STATUS example; headers.
failure-path: probe target hangs for 10 s -> request still returns in < 3 s.
security test: error responses contain no connection strings or internal hostnames.
guardrails: MUST NOT touch any dependency in `/healthz`.
MUST NOT expose internal hostnames, IPs, version numbers of dependencies or error messages in `/readyz` or `/v1/status`.
MUST bound every probe with a timeout (2 s) and the readiness checks with 1 s each; no unbounded waits.
MUST NOT let status failures block local or LAN use; the feed is informational (clients must not gate on it).
MUST keep incident text free of customer data; the service validates length (<= 500 chars per update).
failure_modes: Redis unavailable -> `/readyz` 503, `/v1/status` serves in-process last snapshot (<= 5 min) then reports components as `degraded` with a synthetic marker, never 500.
Probe flapping -> hysteresis of 3 failures before `major_outage` and 2 successes before recovery.
